q: How should a Rajahmundry pulp mill count CO2 from burning black liquor?
title: Black liquor CO2 at a pulp mill
short: As biogenic, reported separately from Scope 1, because the carbon in black liquor comes from the wood. Methane and nitrous oxide from the recovery boiler stay in Scope 1, as do coal and oil burnt in power boilers and the lime kiln. Make-up limestone adds fossil process CO2.
audience: Integrated pulp and paper mills around Rajahmundry

ul: Recovery boiler: biogenic CO2, plus small methane and nitrous oxide in Scope 1.

p: CO2 released when lime mud is reburnt comes from carbon that started in the wood, so common pulp and paper guidance treats it as biogenic. Fresh limestone bought in is fossil.
Black liquor solids fired, fuel to each boiler and kiln, and limestone purchases by month.
